gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured weight for any wallet option. MacRumors (Eric Slivka) put the ESR Geo Wallet Stand on a scale: 84 g empty and 107 g holding a driver's license, a credit card and an Apple Card. The same article gives 32 g for Apple's MagSafe Wallet empty.
standout_why: I opened three rival pages. Macworld's best-iPhone-17-cases page gives no weight, thickness, drop height or magnet figure. TechGearLab's best-iPhone-case page picks the Wallet Slayer Vol. 1 as best wallet case and ran a MagSafe weight-until-failure retention test, but prints no figures for any wallet, describing the Slayer only as 'Thicker overall'. iphoneipadreview.com says 'Weight and exact thickness: not listed' and adds that it did not test the products itself. I could not check five rivals. Good Housekeeping (cited), Wirecutter (cited), Wired, Travel + Leisure and BestProducts all refused fetches, and I did not try Esquire. So I can't rule out that one of them prints a weight or a pull figure, and that is why this is not a 3.
decides: It doesn't change the pick, but it puts a number on the cost of the detachable route. The ESR Geo Wallet Stand, with its stand and Find My module, weighs 84 g empty against 32 g for Apple's wallet, about 2.6 times as much (MacRumors, March 2023). MacRumors also calls the ESR 'more than twice as thick'. That is weight a shopper picking Find My over a slim one-piece Wallet Slayer would carry. I found no independent pull-force measurement, so the 'slips off' catch on Apple's wallet and ESR's stronger-magnet claims stay unmeasured.
